name: Haritaki
actions: One of the three fruits of triphala
kitchenUse: Not a kitchen herb; a little powder is taken with warm water at bedtime, often as part of triphala.

typicalUse.adultAmount: 3–6 g of powder a day, per classical sources

cautions.note: Avoid in pregnancy; it is a laxative.
Avoid during diarrhoea or with dehydration, weakness or after fasting.

interactions.effect: As a laxative it can reduce absorption of medicines taken at the same time; take them apart.

evidence.summary: Mostly laboratory and animal studies; small human studies of triphala, of which it is part.

sources.title: The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India, Part I
